summary: L-4 ground house on Olallie Mountain, Willamette NF, Oregon; build year disputed (1930-1932); burned in 2019, cause under investigation; the FS trail still reaches the summit.

facts.status_note: Burned in 2019; no source describes what, if anything, remains on the summit

staffing.status: not staffed for many years; last used for emergencies in the 1970s (firelookout.com)

access.note: Forest Service trail #4100 runs to the top of Olallie Mountain; the agency asks visitors to contact the local ranger station for current trail conditions

visit.trail_note: From Pat Saddle Trailhead, take Olallie Trail #3529 south 2 miles to reach trail #4100, which begins a steep climb to the summit

corrections.why: The NHLR 'Removed' field is a register-status date; the NHLR itself says the tower burned in 2019, and the Forest Service confirms the fire.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Not settled. NHLR gives 1930, firelookout.com gives 1932, and Rex's quotes a September 1931 newspaper report that a new cabin had just been completed. The story reports all three.
Forest Service says the lookout burned in fall 2019; Rex's gives an undetermined date in the winter season. The record uses 2019 with the cause under investigation.

notes_for_editor: Build year is disputed across four sources (1930, 1931, 1932; a 1933 date appears in a Facebook group post seen only as a search snippet, not read, not used). The Statesman Journal 2020 article returned HTTP 403 and was not read. Rex's page is a hobby site quoting old newspapers; quotes were checked against its page text, not the original papers. Brief access was unknown; facts.access is public from the FS trail page, which gives no closure information for the summit. No source describes what remains on the summit, and the story says so. No new photos added.
